question: Should OpenClaw retain the proposed all-or-nothing legacy beta DSSE envelope compatibility path while accepting ClawHub’s standard DSSE envelopes at the signed catalog trust boundary?
rationale: This is a deliberate compatibility and trust-policy choice; code review can confirm the branch shape but cannot independently choose the durable acceptance contract for signed producer data.

options.title: Confirm compatibility and require live proof
options.body: Keep the bounded legacy parser, require redacted producer-to-consumer runtime evidence, then review the exact head for merge.

options.title: Standard-only cutover
options.body: Remove legacy beta-envelope acceptance and coordinate a producer/consumer cutover if compatibility is no longer required.

options.title: Pause for specification alignment
options.body: Hold this PR until the Hosted Feed/RFC contract explicitly defines the beta transition and retirement policy.

recommendation.title: Confirm compatibility and require live proof
recommendation.body: Keep the bounded legacy parser, require redacted producer-to-consumer runtime evidence, then review the exact head for merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked feed work identifies this contributor as the available protocol-stack contact for clarifying the producer transition, though final acceptance remains an OpenClaw owner decision.
